stage1.impression: A clean, well-separated studio catalogue shot: the blue horn reads beautifully, with real transmission and a crisp rim, and the cabinet's translucency and internals are legible. But it still reads as a render. The surfaces look smeared and painterly at full size, the pale lining blocks are the brightest thing on the speaker and pull the eye from the horn, the paper goes a muddy grey in the upper left, and the cabinet sits on the floor with almost no weight and none of its blue light thrown onto the paper.

blocking_9: Clean full-resolution surfaces: no denoiser smear or painterly banding on the horn interior, cloth disc or acrylic edges
The cabinet visibly grounded: a soft footprint shadow at least 15% darker than the open floor, extending 0.2-0.3 m around the base
The tinted acrylic throwing a visible blue (colour-matched) transmitted glow onto the paper in front of the base
An even, clean paper sweep with no dingy grey corner: upper-left within about 30 levels of upper-right
The horn as the brightest, first-read element; the lining band no longer the brightest area on the product
Lining and cover cloth reading as real textile (out of scope here, but they block a 9)

defects.what: Paper sweep goes a muddy grey in the upper left (lum 157-162) while the upper right is near white (235). The diagonal gradient reads as dirty, not designed
Footprint shadow too weak: just in front of the base the floor is 174 against 181 on open floor. Only a thin core line grounds the cabinet, so it looks light and slightly placed
No coloured transmitted light on the paper: the floor is neutral grey (R171 G183 B190, the same as open floor), so the translucent blue acrylic casts no blue onto the ground
Upper lining band is the brightest area on the product (median 209, blue channel 251, 1.2% clipped). It competes with the horn and reads as a foam block
Denoiser smear / watercolour texture and soft banding in the horn's interior and around the throat
Cloth disc reads as a flat matte painted disc, with no weave or fibre (shader, out of scope)
Right side panel is heavy and dark for Ice (median 97, R50). It reads as dense navy glass rather than pale translucent blue
Bottom edges of the cabinet crush to near black navy (p5 lum 8 on the left face), so the base edge looks heavy
Horn bezel's top edge carries a dull grey line that reads as a dirty edge rather than a polished resin lip

changes.problem: Surfaces read as smeared and painterly (denoiser artefacts and banding), the main thing that says 'render'.

evidence.measured: 3x crop shows watercolour-like blotching on the horn interior and soft banding around the throat; the same smear is on the cloth disc and the acrylic edges

change.to: 1024 samples at full size (1080 x 2160), with the denoiser on albedo+normal prefilter 'accurate' or blended at 50%; keep finish grain 1.5

changes.expected: Fine, photographic micro-detail on the resin and acrylic, no blotches; the grain sits on real detail instead of over smear.

changes.problem: The translucent blue cabinet throws no coloured light onto the paper, so the product's best material quality never touches the set.

evidence.measured: floor in front of base R171 G183 B190, the same balance as the open floor at left (R178 G188 B193)

change.to: add 'sweep' (and raise lights.back elevation from 20 to 30 so the light passes through the cabinet and lands 0.1-0.4 m in front of the base)

changes.expected: A soft blue-tinted glow on the paper just in front of and beside the base. For the sister colours the glow takes each tint (neutral for Fog, dark for Smoke).

changes.problem: The cabinet has almost no footprint shadow, so it lacks weight.

evidence.measured: lum_median 174 against 181 on open floor at [170,990,380,1040]: only 4% darker beyond a thin core

change.to: strength 1.0, distance_m 0.32 (core unchanged); and lower lights.pool from 1.5 to 1.0 W/m2 so it stops washing out the footprint

changes.expected: A soft shadow about 0.3 m deep around the base, darkest at the contact line, fading into the paper.

changes.problem: The upper-left paper is a muddy grey against a near-white right, which looks dingy on a narrow colour card.

evidence.measured: lum_median 162 against 235 at [440,0,540,150]; the left-edge profile rises 157 to 210 down the frame

changes.expected: The sweep falls off gently from right to left. The upper left lands at 195-215, keeping some separation behind the lit left face without going grey.

changes.problem: The upper lining band is the brightest area on the speaker and pulls the eye away from the horn.

evidence.measured: lum_median 209, b_median 251, clip 1.2%; horn interior [100,290,200,420] is only 146

change.to: remove 'lining-*' from lights.back and lights.kick receivers; back irradiance 3.0 to 2.4

changes.expected: The lining reads as soft white behind the acrylic, a step below the horn's highlights, with nothing clipped.

changes.problem: The right side panel is heavy, dense navy rather than pale translucent Ice.
changes.expected: The side panel brightens to a translucent mid blue with a soft vertical gradient, still clearly the shadow side.

changes.problem: The base edges crush to near black navy, which makes the bottom of the cabinet heavy.

change.to: shrink to 1.6 x 2.4 m and move to [1.6, 1.8, 0.005] so the lower edges pick up some paper reflection

changes.expected: The lower edges keep a dark line but open to deep blue instead of black.

out_of_scope.request: Give the cover cloth a visible weave and fibre
out_of_scope.why: It reads as a flat painted disc. The cloth shader is being reworked elsewhere.

out_of_scope.request: Give the white lining batts textile texture (voile sleeve, quilting)
out_of_scope.why: They read as smooth pale foam blocks, the main thing that cheapens the cabinet's interior. The lining shaders are being reworked elsewhere.

out_of_scope.request: Clean up the dull grey line on the horn's top lip
out_of_scope.why: It is part of the speaker's resin model and material.

out_of_scope.request: Lighten the dark mass at the horn's throat
out_of_scope.why: 53% crushed, but the card fixes it as the resin's own depth.
